subtopics.title: The Cast of Symbols and the Four Equations

questions.question: The equations of motion may only be used when:
options: The object moves in a circle

questions.question: Which quantity is missing from the equation vf² = vi² + 2aΔx?
The 'absent character' rule for choosing an equation says:
options: Pick the equation that excludes the quantity which is neither given nor wanted
Pick the equation with the most known symbols

subtopics.title: Choosing the Equation and Finding the Acceleration

questions.question: For the bakkie problem (vi = 8 m/s, vf = 20 m/s, Δx = 210 m, find a), the absent quantity is:
options: Displacement — so use vf = vi + aΔt
Final velocity — so use equation two

questions.question: Substituting into vf² = vi² + 2aΔx gives 400 = 64 + 420a. The acceleration is:
options: 0,8 m/s² in the direction of motion

questions.question: Why must the direction be stated with the acceleration answer?

subtopics.title: Finding the Time — Two Roads to One Answer

questions.question: Using vf = vi + aΔt with a = 0,8 m/s², the time taken is:
The check via Δx = ½(vi + vf)Δt uses the average velocity, which is:
Why is the second road (equation four) such a strong check on the first?
options: It uses only original given data, so an error in the calculated acceleration could not hide
It is always quicker to compute

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: A bakkie travels at 72 km/h. Before using the equations of motion, this must become:
In vf² = vi² + 2aΔx, a common error is:
options: Forgetting to square the velocities — writing 20 instead of 400

questions.question: If the bakkie had been braking, the acceleration in your equations would be:
options: Negative (opposite to the chosen positive direction of motion)

questions.question: In Grade 12, these same equations reappear in vertical projectile motion, where the constant acceleration is:
options: Zero at the top of the flight

questions.question: The five facts that describe any straight-line trip are:
options: Speed, mass, distance, force and time
Starting speed, final speed, acceleration, time and displacement
Velocity, direction, distance, fuel and time
Position, speed, weight, time and route

questions.question: The word 'uniformly' in a question is important because:
options: It means the road is straight
It means the speed is constant
It is your permission to use the equations at all — the acceleration must be steady
It guarantees the distance is a round number

questions.question: An acceleration of 0,8 m/s² means, in plain words:
options: The bakkie gains 0,8 metres per second of extra speed in each second
The bakkie covers 0,8 metres every second
The bakkie takes 0,8 seconds to reach top speed
The bakkie's speed is 0,8 of the speed limit

questions.question: Which equation has NO acceleration in it?
options: Final speed equals starting speed plus acceleration times time
Distance equals starting speed times time plus half the acceleration times time squared
Final speed squared equals starting speed squared plus two times acceleration times distance
Distance equals the average of the two speeds times the time

subtopics.title: The One Fact You Don't Need

questions.question: In the bakkie problem, which fact does nobody mention and nobody ask for?
After substituting, 400 = 64 + 420 × acceleration. The next step is:
options: Subtract 64 from both sides, then divide by 420

questions.question: Why does 0,8 m/s² pass the sense check while 80 m/s² would not?
options: Because answers must be smaller than one
Because gaining just under a metre per second of speed each second is an ordinary pull-away

questions.question: The plain-language choosing rule is:
options: Find the fact nobody mentioned, then take the equation that leaves it out
Use the equation containing the wanted quantity twice
Try every equation until one gives a round number

questions.question: The bakkie goes smoothly from 8 m/s to 20 m/s, so its average speed for the trip is:
Using 210 m = 14 m/s × time, the time taken is:
Why is the change-counting comparison a good description of the two roads?
options: Because two independent counts that agree are worth far more than one confident count
Because you should always divide twice
Because the second road is faster

questions.question: Seventy-two kilometres per hour is 72 000 metres in 3 600 seconds, which is:
options: 20 m/s — which is why you divide km/h by 3,6
